header: What a charge costs (23 Nov 2026), from the OFFICIAL rules and nothing else; every figure here was read from the document named beside it. Pure; nothing is stored or sent. A PUBLIC CHARGER'S PRICE per unit (kWh) is, by the Ministry of Power's guidelines (clause 8 lists the parts): the electricity tariff the station pays + a SERVICE CHARGE + land cost + GST. Here:

* the electricity tariff is West Bengal's: WBERC's order of 20 March 2025 for WBSEDCL, tariff year 2025-26, paragraph "Promotional tariff for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations": "Rs. 6.00 per unit during the 'peak' hours (17:00 hrs to 23:00 hrs) and Rs. 5.50 per unit during 'other than peak' hours shall continue". This is the NEWEST order the WBERC's own list shows (checked 22 Nov 2026: nothing for 2026-27); a newer order changes these two numbers, and a person can type the rate they actually pay (ownRate below).

* the service charge is the CEILING of the Ministry of Power's Guidelines for Installation and Operation of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure-2024 (17 September 2024), clause 10(1): AC (slow) Rs 3.00 in the solar hours (9:00 am to 4:00 pm) and Rs 4.00 in the non-solar hours (4:00 pm to 9:00 am); DC (fast) Rs 11.00 and Rs 13.00; "till 31st March, 2028"; "subject to annual review"; GST and land cost excluded. So the figure I show is the HIGHEST a station may charge per unit before GST and land cost, not a price any one station promises. A station may charge less.

At home: "Domestic electricity rates will apply to charging EVs at home" (the same guidelines, clause 15(4)). The domestic rate depends on the household's slab, so there is no single figure to show: the person types the rate on their own bill. The same box takes the price printed on a charger's display; whatever is typed replaces the standard figures. Units charged for: the energy drawn, which is the energy added to the battery divided by the efficiency of the charging (ev.ts: AC 90%, DC 95%).

doc: The sources, in the words of the card.

behaviours: West Bengal: Rs 6.00 in the peak hours, Rs 5.50 in the others
the service charge ceilings: AC 3 and 4, DC 11 and 13
three times of day: day, evening, night
the peak electricity tariff goes with the evening only, the lower service charge with the day only
a fast charger is dearer than a slow one at every time of day
AC by day: 32 kWh added, 35.56 units drawn at Rs 8.50 is about Rs 302
DC by day: 33.68 units drawn at Rs 16.50 is about Rs 556
the standard figure says its two parts
the evening costs more than the day, for the same charge
a typed rate (a home bill, a charger's display) replaces the standard: 35.56 units at Rs 7 is Rs 248.92
an unusable rate (zero, negative, text, over Rs 100, not a number) is ignored: the standard figures are used
rates are written with two decimals
every figure has its source: the WBERC order of 20 March 2025 and the Ministry of Power guidelines of 17 September 2024, with the validity and the review
the file states what it is not: a ceiling, not a station's promise; GST and land cost excluded
